name: Nguluka
body:
NGULUKA
CR 2

Iridescent feathers cloak a birdlike body, but its neck and head are those of a hooded cobra. Its serpentine eyes gleam a baleful red.

XP 600
N Small magical beast
Init +2; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +6

DEFENSE

AC 14, touch 13, flat-footed 12 (+2 Dex, +1 natural, +1 size)
hp 22 (3d10+6)
Fort +5, Ref +5, Will +2

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., fly 40 ft. (clumsy)
Melee bite +6 (1d4–2 plus poison)
Special Attacks deadly gaze, poison

STATISTICS

Str 7, Dex 14, Con 15, Int 6, Wis 12, Cha 5
Base Atk +3; CMB +0; CMD 12
Feats Ability Focus (deadly gaze), Weapon Finesse
Skills Fly +0, Perception +6
Languages one language if trained (cannot speak)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Deadly Gaze (Su)

Living creatures within 30 feet meeting the nguluka’s gaze gain 1 temporary negative level (DC 14 Will negates), lasting for 1 hour. A creature can gain no more than 4 negative levels from nguluka gazes. A creature with 4 negative levels that fails its save against the nguluka’s gaze drops to –1 hit points and is dying. This is a mind-affecting effect and the save DC is Wisdom-based.

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 13; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d2 Con; cure 2 consecutive saves.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate and warm forests
Organization solitary, pair, muster (3–5), or ostentation (6–10)
Treasure none

A nguluka is a hideous hybrid of an oversized guineafowl and a forest cobra. It makes its lairs deep in thickest parts of the forest, living either in fig trees or caves. It enjoys the flesh of mammals and birds, and the bones of such creatures litter its lair. It likes nothing more than ripe figs and tends to come out at night to search for the succulent fruit. Many creatures that meet the gaze of a nguluka die immediately, but those that don’t often die from its highly venomous bite.

Few escape an encounter with a nguluka alive.

While unpleasant of disposition at the best of times, nguluka can be trained by those with a great deal of patience and skill.

People who are blind cannot be killed by the nguluka’s gaze, so they are the most likely to employ these creatures as guards.

Legends tell of circles of blind druids or monasteries full of blind monks that employ nguluka as guardians.
